competencies.statement: I know the main personal gear to bring on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate in list form the items of clothing they need to bring with them for a camping event. The Scout should be encouraged to collect and pack their equipment. Spare clothing. Equipment. Wash gear. Wet weather clothing. Repair equipment. Sleeping equipment.

competencies.statement: I know how to care for my personal camping gear
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to show an awareness of the value of camping equipment. A Scout should demonstrate how to go about checking and caring for equipment. Safety implications of poor or faulty equipment. Keeping personal equipment in working order. How to sew. How to repair items of equipment. The quality of different items of equipment.

competencies.statement: I know what clothes I should bring on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should know what clothes they need to bring on camp and talk about the clothing needs for different weather conditions. Layer system. Outer shell - wet weather gear.

competencies.statement: I know how to set out my sleeping area for a good night‘s sleep
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be aware of the need for tidiness, insulation and warmth. Sleeping area, pillow, sleeping mat. Pack away clothes. Tidy rucksack, select clothes for next day use.

competencies.statement: I know the different emergency services that are available and how and when to call them
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain how to call out the emergency services when an accident takes place on the mountains (Police, Ambulance). They should know when and how they should call for the mountain rescue service rather than any of the other of the emergency services.

competencies.statement: I know the main parts of a tent
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know the main parts of a tent and there use and names. While there are many types of tents, the key features are common, for example the ridge, the guys, door flaps, wall, vents, sod clo groundsheet. This Scout should be able to point out the parts on an erected tent on a camp rather than from a picture in a book.

competencies.statement: I have spent at least one night on camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout will have attended their first Scout Camp and have slept in a tent on that camp as a Scout. For the purpose of this requirement, nights spent camping with their family are not permissible.

competencies.statement: I can collect small sticks suitable for a fire making.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to go off in search of firewood and return with suitable dry wood for lighting a fire. A Scout should be able to identify suitable wood to use for tinder, light sticks and long burning logs.

competencies.statement: I know about the Buddy system
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to talk about the buddy system and explain how and why it is used when camping.

competencies.statement: I can help pitch a tent
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate they wish to complete this requirement so that they can be observed in action with other Scouts.

competencies.statement: I can pack my rucksack for camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to bring a packed rucksack for demonstration and discuss, while unpacking and repacking, the value of the method used in the packing process. The necessary equipment to pack. Where to place soft items. Where to place heavy items. Where to place foodstuffs. What is meant by ‘first in last out’. What wet weather clothing to bring.

competencies.statement: I can keep my camping gear neat and tidy while on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to demonstrate an awareness of camp-life (living on camp and sleeping in tents) and the need to keep things tidy, so a comfortable life in a tent and around a campsite is possible. Scouts should also be aware of the conditions around a campsite and the implications of untidiness in bad weather conditions. Scouts need to have camped for at least one night to be in a position to understand the answers they may have to provide to fulfil the requirements of this badge. 8 15/02/2010 21:47:07 Camping

competencies.statement: I know about the food pyramid and can discuss it with a Scouter
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show knowledge in the creation of a basic menu with reference to the food pyramid. What food forms the bottom layer of the pyramid. What foods forms the mid sections of the pyramid. What food forms the top layer. List the best food to choose from each layer. ndb 9

competencies.statement: I know about safe food storage and hygiene
competencies.explanation: Scouts should show an understanding of the differences between camp and home and how it can affect the storage of food. They should also be capable of demonstrating how to store food in a safe manner. That food is prepared without electrical household appliances and gadgets. That food is more likely to be exposed to flies and insects and stored in containers. That food needs to be cooked properly.

competencies.statement: I can get a weather forecast
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be aware of where they can th, obtain a weather forecast ( newspaper, radio/TV, web site) and how it might impact on the plans for the camp

competencies.statement: I can help prepare food for cooking on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to show in a practical way how food is prepared for cooking. This can be done as part of a cooking team or assisting a more experienced cook. How to clean food. How to prepare food properly.

competencies.statement: I know how I would get help if someone is hurt
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to show an ability to recognize that someone is hurt badly and needs help. The Scout should also know how to get help and by what means.

competencies.statement: I know how to behave safely around fires
competencies.explanation: The Scouts should show an understanding of the dangers of fire and how to behave around fires. Do not play around a fire. Do not poke a fire. Keep a safe distance from the fire. Obey the instruction of the fire tender. 9 15/02/2010 21:47:07 How to repair items of equipment. The quality of different items of equipment.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate my understanding of the fire triangle
competencies.explanation: The Scout should discuss the qualities of each part of the fire triangle and demonstrate on a fire the effect of each element if it is removed from the triangle.

competencies.statement: I know how to be safe while cooking
competencies.explanation: The necessity to prepare and cook a meal will involve the Scout in situations where care and attention are required. The rules and use of knives. Lifting hot liquids, foods from a cooking stove or the fire . Scouts should be able to demonstrate and talk through the safety processes . I understand why I should follow directions from an instructor. The Scout should know about the importance of listening to the instructor so that they are aware of what to do and the dangers of doing things that they don’t fully understand.

competencies.statement: I understand why I should follow directions frm an instructor.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know about the importance of listening to the instructor so that they are aware of what to do and the dangers of doing things that they don’t fully understand.

competencies.statement: I have spent at least two nights on camp (outside)
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to have camped under canvas for at least two night to be in a position to understand the answers they may have provided to fulfil the requirements of this badge.

competencies.statement: I know how to care for all my personal gear
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to show an awareness of the value of camping equipment. They should also be aware that if it is not working properly it is likely to fail in b weather conditions. A scout should demonstrate how to go about checking and caring for equipment. Safety implications of poor or faulty equipment. Keeping personal equipment in working order. How to sew. How to repair items of equipment. The quality of different items of equipment.

competencies.statement: I know how to store food on camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to demonstrate and discuss how to go about setting up a store tent or organising food storage on a campsite. The Scout should be aware of use of containers and covers as well as an awareness of heat in tents and cold storage locations.

competencies.statement: I can help make a hot drink on the fire
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate they wish to complete this requirement so that they can be observed in action. Safety, attention to detail and awareness of fire, heat and hot liquids should be observed.

competencies.statement: I can help clean up a fireplace after camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should assist other members in the tidying up and the cleaning of a fireplace or designated fire lighting area. This will involve the careful disposal of ashes, replacing stones, or deconstruction of an altar fire. Leave No Trace should be evident; there should be no evidence that a fire has been lit in this location after the task is completed (except in a designated fire light area on a campsite in that case it should be left in a suitable state for the next campers).

competencies.statement: I know how weather can affect our camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to know what to do if it rains or it is very hot, forward thinking and being prepared. Explain the different types of weather likely to occur. Explain what will happen if it rains in the camp area. Explain what will happen if it is very hot Explain what extra gear you need to bring - just in case.

competencies.statement: I know why I bring certain gear on camp for our team
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show an awareness of the need for general patrol e quipment and be able to list the main items required and how they differ from personal equipment. Tentage - sleeping, dining, storage. Storage. First aid. Cooking utensils. Tools.

competencies.statement: I can use camp tools safely on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should show how to use a tool correctly and also be aware of any safety implications. Be able to use a tool correctly to do the job it was designed for. Display your skill in using a particular tool. Know how to store the tools away for use at another time.

competencies.statement: I know how to clean and treat a small cut or scratch
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to talk themselves through the process of treatment. This demonstration/talk can be done in a practical way on a volunteer. How to clean the wound. How to reassure the casualty. How to apply a bandage.

competencies.statement: I can show a younger Scout how to pitch a tent with the help of others
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate they wish to complete this requirement so that they can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I can assist in the cooking of a meal while on camp
competencies.explanation: A Scout should act as an assistant to another more experienced cook. They should assist in preparation, cooking and serving of a simple hot meal on camp. The Scout should display confidence and basic cooking knowledge.

competencies.statement: I know the main principles of ‘Leave No Trace'
competencies.explanation: Scouts should demonstrate an understanding of the key points in a practical way in camp situations. Dispose of waste properly. Respect farm animals and wildlife. Minimise camping impact and the effects of fire. Be considerate of others. Travel and camp on durable surfaces. Leave what you find. Plan ahead and prepare.

competencies.statement: I can help others to learn about camping
competencies.explanation: The Scout should display a willingness to help others learn in a natural way. The Scout should be observed in action over a period of time rather than mount a single display of expertise.

competencies.statement: I have spend at least two nights consecutive lightweight camping
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to have camped under canvas for at least two nights (over a weekend) to be in a position to understand the answers they may have provided to fulfil the requirements of this badge.

competencies.statement: I know what personal gear I would bring on a lightweight and a standing camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate in list form the items of clothing they need to bring with them for various camping activities, over a number of days. Scouts need to be aware of the need for proper clothing in all weather conditions. The weight of the pack is also a concern and Scouts should be pointing out weight saving measures with consideration for safety particularly with reference to lightweight and standing camping. Scouts should indicate in list form the items of clothing they need to bring with them for various camping events. The Scout should also show an interest in the quality of equipment design and its benefits. Spare clothing. Eating gear. Wash gear. Wet weather equipment. Repair equipment. Sleeping equipment

competencies.statement: I can pack a rucksack properly for a lightweight camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to bring a packed rucksack for discussion. The Scouts should then demonstrate and discuss while unpacking and repacking the value of the method used in the packing process. Weight of pack is a major consideration. This should be balanced against necessary equipment and luxury items. The necessary equipment to pack. Where to place soft items. Where to place heavy items. Where to place foodstuffs. What is meant by ‘first in last out’. What wet weather equipment to bring.

competencies.statement: I know how to user our Team gear correctly and safely
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to demonstrate basic procedures for cleaning and the care for equipment. Demonstrate how to use patrol equipment safely. Demonstrate how to clean, care for and store tools,tentage and cooking equipment when not in use.

competencies.statement: I know how to care for our Team equipment during and in between camp.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to demonstrate basic procedures for cleaning and care and storage of equipment during camping adventures . Demonstrate how to clean, care for and store tools, tentage and cooking equipment when not in use

competencies.statement: I know the best place to pitch a tent and explain why
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to show where a tent should be pitched and why that spot was chosen. Scouts should mention level ground, wind direction, shelter, and tree coverage. Site layout on a fixed camp. Location of fireplace. Prevailing wind.

competencies.statement: I know how to use and store tools safely
competencies.explanation: Scout should show how to use a tool correctly and also be aware of any safety implications. Be able to use a tool correctly to do the job it was designed for. Display your skill in using a particular tool. Know how to store the tools away for use at another time.

competencies.statement: I know what to do in the case of cuts and minor burns
competencies.explanation: The prime consideration for a Scout to demonstrate is that they know the rules of First Aid. Treatment of minor cuts, burns is always subject to adult or medical advice and if in doubt they should seek help. In the case of minor treatments these should be demonstrated in a practical way with a volunteer casualty. State the rules of First aid. Demonstrate how to treat a minor cut. Discuss what they would do in the case of a minor burn or scald and demonstrate treatment. Discuss how they would take care of the victim. Discuss what they would tell a medical person when calling for help.

competencies.statement: I can be safe around fires and cooking equipment
competencies.explanation: The Scouts should show an understanding of the dangers of fire and how to behave around fires. Do not play around a fire. Do not poke a fire. Keep a safe distance from the fire. Obey the instruction of the fire tender. The necessity to prepare and cook a meal will involve the Scout in situations where care and attention are required. The rules and use of knives. Lifting hot liquids, foods from a cooking stove or the fire. Scouts should be able to demonstrate and talk through the processes

competencies.statement: I can be a constructive member of my Team while on camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout should participate on camp as a full member of the Team. The Scout should take part in, and play a number of roles while on camp and generally add to the well being of the whole Team.

competencies.statement: I can assist in the pitching of a tent with my Team
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate they wish to complete this requirement so that they can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I know what Team equipment to bring on various types of camps
competencies.explanation: The Scout should produce in list form the patrol equipment necessary for a variety of camps. The Scout should discuss how each item is relevant and also the essential safety equipment that is required. With regards to a lightweight camp the Scout should discuss how the weight load might be distributed among the Team.

competencies.statement: I can plan a balanced menu with my ‘Team’ for a camping adventure

competencies.statement: I have spent at least four nights on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to have camped under canvas for at least four nights (over a number of weekends or on a single camping adventure) to be in a position to have the experience, knowledge and understanding to answers they may have provided to fulfil the requirements of this badge

competencies.statement: I know what you need for building shelters and bivvy’s
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to list the items and tools required to build a bivouac shelter. The Scout should have participated in the building of such a structure The roof should be made of plastic sheeting and not ferns and leaves. Basic roof structure using materials found on the ground not cut down. Refer to the ‘ Leave No Trace’ principles.

competencies.statement: I can explain how you choose the best type of tent for your specific camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to ascertain the quality of a tent design and the type of camping best suited to a particular design. The Scout should also have the capability to recognize the appropriate tentage for the needs of the group on a specific camping expedition.

competencies.statement: I know how to store and cook food safely on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should show an understanding of the differences between camp and home. They should also be capable of demonstrating how to do it. A Scout should also be aware of the need to cook food properly to prevent sickness. How to minimize the handling of food. How to ensure food is cooked through. How food is cooked properly and edible (not burnt.) How food is stored on camp. ndb 13

competencies.statement: I know what Team equipment to bring on various types of camps
competencies.explanation: The Scout should produce in list form the patrol equipment necessary for a variety of camps. The Scout should discuss how each item is relevant and also the essential safety equipment that is required. With regards to a lightweight camp the Scout should discuss how the weight load might be distributed among the Team.

competencies.statement: I can plan a balanced menu with my ‘Team’ for a camping adventure
competencies.explanation: The Scout should approach this requirement via interaction with his/her Team in the planning of menus. The menus suggested should acknowledge

competencies.statement: I can select a suitable location for a standing or lightweight camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to show where a tent should be pitched and why that spot was chosen. Scouts should mention level ground, wind direction, shelter, and tree coverage. Site layout on a fixed camp. Location of fireplace or stove for cooking. Prevailing wind.

competencies.statement: I can show the best lay out for your Team campsite
competencies.explanation: The Scout should have camped a number of times and be aware of how a campsite is laid out with a view to prevailing winds, walkways, fireplace location and tentage considerations. Location of sleeping area. Location of fire & kitchen area. Location of dining area.

competencies.statement: I can use at least two different types of cooking fires and stoves
competencies.explanation: The Scouts needs to have been involved in a number of cooking situations. This is best demonstrated in a camp situation where the Scout can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I can give a weather report to my Scouter for while we are on camp
competencies.explanation: Weather is always a consideration on camp. Scouts need to demonstrate knowledge of how to obtain weather forecast for the area they are camping in. The Scout in presenting the weather report should :- Explain the different types of weather likely to occu Explain what will happen if it rains in the camp area Explain what will happen if it is very hot. Explain what extra gear you need to bring - just in case.

competencies.statement: I can show the best place on camp for a chopping pit
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to demonstrate an understanding of what happens or is likely to happen in a chopping area. Clear chopping area. Overhead obstructions.

competencies.statement: I can show a younger Scout how to pitch a tent
competencies.explanation: This is a practical exercise. It can be done with hel from Team members. In demonstrating the skill they should direct other Team members to complete the task.

competencies.statement: I know how to pitch tents correctly for bad weather conditions
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to show where a tent should be pitched and why that spot was chosen. Scouts should mention level ground, drainage, wind direction, shelter, and tree coverage. Scouts should also be able to demonstrate additional ‘storm’ measures that may be necessary. Site layout on a fixed camp. Location of fireplace. Prevailing wind. Storm procedures and measures. I understand the importance of proper waste

competencies.statement: I understand the importance of proper waste management on camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show an understanding of how to camp in a ‘Leave No Trace’ manner and the waste that could be generated in a camp situation. The Scout should explain what to do with waste water, refuse, waste food matter and recycling where appropriate.

competencies.statement: I can light and maintain a cooking fire
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to demonstrate this skill over a number of fire lighting situations. This is best done in a camp situation where the Scout can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I know how to cook a proper meal on a fire.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to cook a full hot meal, assisted by another Scout perhaps. This meal should be considered a ‘dinner’ meal rather than a lunch or breakfast so that the Scout can demonstrate their cooking skills to the fullest

competencies.statement: I have spent at least five consecutive nights on camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to have camped under canvas for at least five nights on a single camping adventure to be in a position to have the experience, knowledge and understanding to answers they may have provided to fulfil the requirements of this badge.

competencies.statement: I have spend at least one night lightweight camping.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have spent at least one night camping in lightweight camping conditions. All camping equipment should have been transported to the ‘wild camping’ site on their backs (in rucksacks). The Scout should also have participated in the organization of such an adventure as part of the team

competencies.statement: I know how to plan the menu and purchase the food for a weekend camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout should approach this requirement via interaction with his/her Team in the planning of menus. The menus suggested should acknowledge the food pyramid. What food forms the bottom layer of the pyramid. What food forms the mid sections of the pyramid. What food forms the top layer. List the best food to choose from each layer to create a balanced diet. In the development of camp budgets and menus the Scout should be aware of the basic quantities of food that are required to feed a patrol without waste. Prepare a basic shopping list for a meal at camp. Discuss the basic or recommended servings per person.

competencies.statement: I can source local knowledge of a campsite and surrounding area
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate a capability of seek information from a number of sources. Before the camp the Scout should have information on the local shops, places to eat, hospital, religiou services etc so they can be availed of on camp. The Scout should also conduct some research into what in the locality of the campsite is of historical, art or geographical interest.

competencies.statement: I know how to plan a programme of activities for a camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to demonstrate knowledge of the different types of activity that are possible on the campsite and how best to maximize the opportunities they present. Variety, fun and adventure as well as off site activities should all play a part. Time tabling as well as equipment considerations need to be displayed.

competencies.statement: I know the causes and how to recognize and treat hypothermia, hyperthermia, sunstroke, dehydration and asthma, or any medical conditions relevant to my team
competencies.explanation: The prime consideration for a Scout to demonstrate is that they know the rules of First Aid. A Scout should be aware of any personal conditions that might exist in the team and have discussed these with the person concerned. The Scout should also be able to list the symptoms of various conditions and know what to do. Discuss the treatment for each ailment. Discuss the special needs of people in their Patrol. Discuss how to prevent these ailments happening.

competencies.statement: I can show how to care for, store and maintain all our Team equipment.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be aware of the need for care to prolong the life of this equipment. Expertise in the basic repair of equipment is expected and procedures for cleaning and care should be known and practiced.

competencies.statement: I can explain what group emergency equipment we should bring on camp and why
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be safety conscious and be able to discuss possible emergency situations that are likely to be encountered. The Scout should also produce a list of the types of equipment that should be present on a campsite. First aid kit. Safety ropes. Survival bag. Emergency shelter.

competencies.statement: I can organise the pitching and striking of a istic
competencies.explanation: Team campsite. This requirement implies that a Scout has some experience and is aware of how they should act, lead and be responsible for a Team and the Group on camp. This is best demonstrated in a camp situation where the Scouts can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I know how to use a variety of stoves in outdoor conditions safely
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to have been involved in a number of cooking situations. This is best demonstrated in a camp situation where the Scout can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I can talk to our Team about the hazards involved in camping
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to list possible hazards at camp and suggest solutions for safer camping. Guy ropes and fencing. Pits and holes. Fires. Chopping areas. Lifting and hauling equipment.

competencies.statement: I can pitch a tent that I am not familiar with
competencies.explanation: Firstly, the Scout must be able to pitch a variety of tents. Secondly, the Scout must be able to pitch the same tents in bad weather. Ideally this will be observed. However, the Scouts should also be able to discuss how they would go about this task in various bad weather situations. The Scout must be able to demonstrate how to pitch any tent presented correctly.

competencies.statement: I have successfully camped in a variety of weather conditions
competencies.explanation: The Scout can have a successful camp no matter what external factors arise.

competencies.statement: I have spend at least eight nights on camp including a week long camp
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to have camped under canvas for at least eight nights on a single camping adventure or combination of camping adventures, one of these should be an annual camp: to be in a position to have the experience, knowledge and understanding to answers they may have provided to fulfil the requirements of this stage. Scouts completing this stage should be experienced campers who have camped in many situations and possess the necessary skills to camp in comfort in any situation. Many Scouts attempting this badge will have camped in excess of the eight nights required.

competencies.statement: I have spend at least two nights consecutive lightweight camping
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have spent at least two night camping in lightweight camping conditions. All camping equipment should have been transported to the ‘wild camping’ site on their backs (in rucksacks). The Scout should also have participated in the organization of such an adventure as part of the team.

competencies.statement: I know how to select a suitable location for both standing and lightweight camps.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should be able to show and discuss why particular locations are suitable for camping and why that spot was chosen. Scouts should mention level ground, drainage, wind direction, shelter, and tree coverage. Consideration should also be demonstrated for the provision of programme activities and adventure locations nearby.

competencies.statement: I can plan and lead a team camp in a wild/ remote location for a minimum of two nights
competencies.explanation: This requirement is undertaken by experienced campers who are also in a leadership position. The camp has to be planned in detail by both the youth leader and the accompanying group. The Scouter has to be fully aware of all plans and satisfy himself/ herself that the Scout is capable of this undertaking.

competencies.statement: I know how to organise the transport required for camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate a capability to seek information from a number of sources. The Scout should be capable of organizing the most suitable transport to and from the campsite.

competencies.statement: I know how to plan activities for various types of camps
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to demonstrate knowledge of the different types of activity that are possible on the campsite, and how best to maximize the opportunities they present. Variety, fun and adventure as well as off site activities should all play a part. Time tabling as well as equipment considerations need to be displayed.

competencies.statement: I know how to make contingency plans for our camp
competencies.explanation: Be Prepared!!. While we expect good weather all the time in reality this is not always the case. The Scout needs to discuss this situation and know the value of have ‘Plan B’ in case of bad weather or other unforeseen situations.

competencies.statement: I can take responsibility for myself and my Team while on camp
competencies.explanation: This requirement implies that a Scout has some experience and is aware of how they should act, lead and be responsible for a Patrol and the Group on camp. This is best demonstrated in a camp situation where the Scouts can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I can help those camping with my Team to learn new skills
competencies.explanation: The Scout is experienced in living outdoors. The Scout should be able to evaluate the ability of fello Scouts, assist where necessary and work together with those of a similar level or knowledge.

competencies.statement: I have spent at least 12 nights on various types of camps, including at least two consecutive nights without a Scouter
competencies.explanation: The Scout attempting this badge will be very experienced and will have camped many times and possess many skills. The Scout should be capable of passing on such skills to other campers and instilling in them the camping spirit and love of the outdoors.

competencies.statement: I can prepare for a specialist expedition and have acquired the necessary skills
competencies.explanation: At this level the Scout may wish to take on expeditions which are of specialist and unique nature. The Scout must be able to plan and organize these expeditions adding whatever skills necessary to their existing skills set.

competencies.statement: I can source, compare and organise various transport options for local and foreign locations
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate a capability of seeking information from a number of sources. The Scout should be capable of organizing the transport to and from the campsite. The advantages of different transport methods. The suppliers of transport. The average cost of hiring or using a transport method.

competencies.statement: I know how to create an exciting expedition while catering for everyone’s needs.
competencies.explanation: The scout should be camable of planning, organizing and running an expedition which everyone on camp will find both fun and challenging. Be able to discuss the abilities of his/her Team. Be able to grade hill walking adventures and be aware of hiking difficulties encountered. Be able to chose a route that is challenging but not dangerous for those taking part. Be able to select suitable programme activities for a weekend and long term camp.

competencies.statement: I know how to be active in the out of doors, without disturbing the balance of nature
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be aware that living and walking through open countryside has an impact of some kind and that we need to minimize this intrusion. The Scout should suggest best practice and discuss how to minimize the impact while also enjoying the outdoor experience. The ‘Leave No Trace’ principles should be fully understood and demonstrated in practical situation on camp and at the break of camp. The Scout should lead the final check and clean up of a campsite on a number of occasions.

competencies.statement: know how to be active in the out of doors,without disturbing the balance of nature.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be aware that living and walking through open countryside has an impact of some kind and that we need to minimize this intrusion. The Scout should suggest best practice and discuss  how to minimize the impact while also enjoying the outdoor experience. The ‘Leave No Trace’ principles should be fully understood and demonstrated in practical situation on camp and at the break of camp. The Scout should lead the final check and clean up of a campsite on a number of occasions

competencies.statement: I have assisted in the organisation of at least two camps either for my Team, another
competencies.explanation: Team in my own Group or in another Group. This is a leadership opportunity and will require expertise in camping, programme planning and organisation. The Scout is expected to assist an experienced camp organizer and learn and gain experience from this encounter.

competencies.statement: I have spend at least 16 nights on various types of camps
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to have camped under canvas for at least 16 nights on single camping adventures or combination of camping adventures, one of which should be an annual camp to be in a position to have the experience, knowledge and understanding to answers they may have provided to fulfil the requirements of this badge. Scouts completing this badge should be experienced campers, who have camped in many situations and possess the necessary skills to camp in comfort in any situation. Eight of these nights need to be consecutive. Many scouts attempting this badge will have camped in excess of the 16 nights required.

competencies.statement: I know how to budget, prepare and manage every aspect of the expedition
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be aware of and demonstrate how to prepare a budget and manage that budget over a camping activity and to achieve a break even situation. Have run or assisted in running a number of adventures. Prepare a cost for a suggested adventure. Act as expedition leader on at least two expeditions.

competencies.statement: I know how to ensure that safety precautions are put in place, without curtailing the fun of your camp
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to demonstrate knowledge of safety, key accident situations and how to put in place preventative measures. Fire areas. Camp hygiene. Storage of food. Proper use of tools

competencies.statement: I can plan and execute, camps and expeditions in all types of locations at home or abroad
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to run, in conjunction with others, successful camps and expeditions no matter how the factors could impinge on possible success or failure.

competencies.statement: I know how to source amenities and local places of interest
competencies.explanation: Before the camp the Scout should have information on the local shops, places to eat, hospital, religious services etc so they can be availed of on camp. The Scout should also conduct some research into what in the locality of the campsite is of historical, artist or geographical interest

competencies.statement: I  know how to use a variety of cooking stoves, and know when each type is most effective.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to have been involved in a number of cooking situations. This is best demonstrated in a camp situation where the Scout can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I have organized and led at least one camp for my Team
competencies.explanation: This requirement is undertaken by experienced campers who maybe accompanying another Scout who is organizing and leading the activity. (see above). The camp has to be planned in detail by both the youth leader and the accompanying group. The Scouter has to be fully aware of all plans and satisfy himself/herself that the Scout is capable of this undertaking.

competencies.statement: I have spent at least 20 nights on various types of camps
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to have camped under canvas for at least twenty nights on single camping adventures or a combination of camping adventures, one of which should be an annual camp to be in a position to have the experience, knowledge and understanding to answers they may have provided to fulfil the requirements of this badge. Scouts completing this badge should be experienced campers who have camped in many situations and possess the necessary skills to camp in comfort in any situation. competencies.statement: I know what kinds of clothes to wear when going out into nature.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate in list form the items of clothing they need to bring with them for a backwoods adventure. Clothes for mucking about in. Clothes for wet weather. Clothes that are warm – winter. Clothes that cover arms and protect from cuts and scratches and sunburn. Headwear.

competencies.statement: I know how to prepare food for cooking.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will explain how to prepare food for cooking without the aid of cooking utensils or preparation table. How to clean food. How to prepare food properly. How to place food on a cooking implement/device.

competencies.statement: I know what a basic survival kit should contain.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should produce a survival kit for examination. It should include at least ten useful items. Each item must have a practical use, some may have more than one use. Each item is of real value and will assist in a survival situation.

competencies.statement: I know how to behave safely around fires.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be aware of the possible dangers and how to prevent them. Do not play around a fire. Do not poke a fire. Keep a safe distance from the fire. Obey the instruction of the fire tender.

competencies.statement: I know how to use hand tools safely.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should discuss and then demonstrate how tools are used safely. Know the types of tools likely to be used on a backwoods adventure. Be able to use a tool correctly to do the job it was designed for. Display your skill in using a particular tool. Know how to store the tools away for use at another time.

competencies.statement: I can build a simple shelter.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate they wish to complete this requirement so that they can be observed in action. A shelter should be built using plastic sheeting, rope and tent pegs. Trees can be used to support the shelter.

competencies.statement: I have participated in at least two backwoods activities.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have attended at least two backwoods activities. These activities can range from simple afternoon sessions to day long activities. At this level it is not necessary for a Scout to have camped out overnight in a shelter or ‘survival or backwoods adventure’, what is required is a practical understanding of the principles and expertise associated with backwoods practice and knowledge.

competencies.statement: I know how to cook some food using tin foil instead of pots and pans.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate at least two methods of using foil for cooking. Preparing a foil meal containing all foodstuffs to be cooked. Fry an egg on a pan made of tin foil and a forked stick and baking a potato.

competencies.statement: I know the important things to remember when building a simple shelter using plastic sheeting.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know how to build a shelter from a plastic sheet and show how to attach guy lines. A shelter big enough to accommodate a small Group. A shelter that uses natural fixtures such as trees. A shelter that will protect users from the elements. A shelter that is ‘tight’ to allow water to run off its roof.

competencies.statement: I know how to treat simple cuts and scratches in a hygienic way.
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to talk themselves through the process of treatment. This demonstration/talk can be done in a practical way on a volunteer. How to clean the wound. How to reassure the casualty. How to apply a bandage.

competencies.statement: I know how to set up a fire place and assist in fire lighting.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to set up a simple ground fire, clearing the ground, setting stone boundaries and gather tinder and sticks for the fire. Prepare the ground by clearing an area near a river bed or an area clear of grass. Know where to place a fire. Collect a variety of wood. Observe a fire lighter in action.

competencies.statement: I can prepare and cook food properly in backwoods conditions.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate they wish to complete this requirement so that they can be observed in action. Cook a backwoods meal using foil. Cook an egg in an orange. Cook a sausage on a stick.

competencies.statement: I know about food storage and hygiene.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will be able to explain how food storage and hygiene are of particular importance on a backwoods adventure. That food is prepared without gadgets / utensils. That food is more likely to be exposed to flies and insects. That food needs to be cooked properly by boiling or heat from a fire. That it is necessary to clean hands, knives and utensils constantly to prevent infection.

competencies.statement: I can use hand tools correctly.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate they wish to complete this requirement so that they can be observed in action. Cut a piece of wood in half using a saw. Cut a piece of string using a knife. Dig a hole with a spade.

competencies.statement: I have attended at least an additional two backwoods activities.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have attended at least two further backwoods activities – to those undertaken in Stage 1). These activities can range from simple afternoon sessions to day long activities. At this stage it is not necessary for a Scout to have camped out overnight in a shelter or ‘survival or backwoods adventure’, what is required is a practical understanding of the principles and expertise associated with backwoods practice and knowledge.

competencies.statement: I know how different weather conditions can affect a backwoods activity.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to show an awareness of how weather can affect an activity and how we need to prepare for it. Explain the different types of weather likely to occur. Explain what will happen if it rains in the camp area. Explain what will happen if it is very hot. Explain what extra gear you need to bring, just in case.

competencies.statement: I know how to get help when someone is in trouble.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to show an ability to recognize that a person is hurt and needs help. The Scout should also know how to get help and by what means. How to recognize that someone is hurt. How to compare injured parts with uninjured parts. Methods of getting help. Methods of caring for someone that is hurt.

competencies.statement: I know the main principles of ‘Leave No Trace’.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should demonstrate an understanding of the key points in a practical way in camp situations. Dispose of waste properly. Respect farm animals and wildlife. Minimise camping impact and the effects of fire. Be considerate of others. Travel and camp on durable surfaces. Leave what you find. Plan ahead and prepare.

competencies.statement: I can build a Patrol shelter.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will need to be observed building shelters and be seen to be a useful member of the Patrol in this venture. The shelter needs to be made from plastic sheeting and big enough for a patrol to sleep in. The shelter should be stable and withstand rough weather. The shelter should be free standing, constructed using light poles and forked staves.

competencies.statement: I can use camp tools safely on camp.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show how to use a tool correctly and also be aware of any safety implications. Be able to use a tool correctly to do the job it was designed for. Display your skill in using a particular tool. Know how to store the tools away for use at another time.

competencies.statement: I know about food storage.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should show an understanding of the differences between camp and home and how it can affect the storage of food. They should also be capable of demonstrating how to do it. That food is prepared without electrical household appliances and gadgets. That food is more likely to be exposed to flies and insects and stored in containers. That food needs to be cooked properly by boiling or heat from a fire.

competencies.statement: I can light a fire using natural tinder, fuzz sticks and matches.
competencies.explanation: Scouts are expected to demonstrate that they can light a fire using natural materials – no paper, firelighters etc. The Scout should be confident in assembling the materials and laying out the fire place. Then they should begin and light the fire. The Scout should be given two matches. If however the matches do not light the fire then additional matches can be given. However, we are seeking ‘skill’ in this requirement that will be carried with them for life. A Scout should practice for a while using only two matches before attempting this requirement.

competencies.statement: I can make a simple fish hook.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should make a series of simple fish hooks from a bent safety pin to a more elaborate bone and thorn based hooks. Binding of the hook to the line is important. It should be secure and be able to hold a wriggling fish.

competencies.statement: I can prepare my own survival kit.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should produce a survival kit for examination. It should include at least ten useful items. Each item must have a practical use, some may have more than one use. Each item is of real value and will assist in a survival situation.

competencies.statement: I can teach another Scout about preparing a survival kit.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will have their own survival kit and be able to show it to a new scout explaining why each item is important and how it might be used. The Scout should be observed teaching the other Scout. This can be verified by others and the Scout who has been taught. Explain the choice of each item and how it would help.

competencies.statement: I have attended at least an additional three backwoods activities.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have attended at least three further backwoods activities – to those undertaken in stage 1). These activities can range from simple afternoon sessions to day long activities. At this level it is not necessary for a Scout to have camped out overnight in a shelter or ‘survival or backwoods adventure’ what is required, is a practical understanding of the principles and expertise associated with backwoods practice and knowledge.

competencies.statement: I know what equipment I need to bring with me on a backwoods activity.
competencies.explanation: Weather in open and exposed places is very different to suburban weather. The Scout needs to show an understanding of this fact and indicate how they should deal with likely weather conditions encountered on an adventure. Discuss what would happen if it was really wet. Discuss what would happen if it was windy. How would you protect yourself from the sun. Discuss also personal equipment. Discuss tools that you would bring.

competencies.statement: I know how to set up a tarp bivvy shelter suitable for two people.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate their skill to erect a tarp based shelter for use by two people. Many different shaped designs are possible and the Scout should discuss the merits of their chosen design.

competencies.statement: I know how to prepare a fire place and light and maintain a fire using minimum resources.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to demonstrate that they can light a fire from scratch and keep the fire going until embers are maintained. Prepare the fire place with minimal impact to the ground. Make fuzz sticks for fire lighting. Collect suitable timber for fire lighting and maintaining a fire till embers are produced. Light a fire using natural materials - no paper - using only two matches.

competencies.statement: I can make simple containers using natural materials.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should present a number of containers that he/she has made from natural materials. This might be done during a backwoods activity or maybe presented for examination having been made at home. Containers may be folded containers, bark based, clay modelled or weaved (baskets etc).

competencies.statement: I know how to treat cuts and minor burns.
competencies.explanation: Treatment of minor cuts, burns or broken bones is always subject to adult or medical advice and if in doubt they should seek help. In the case of minor treatments these should be demonstrated in a practical way with a volunteer casualty. Demonstrate how to treat a minor cut. Discuss how they would take care of the victim. Discuss what they would tell a medical person when summoning help.

competencies.statement: I can make camp bread such as twists and scones.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should make these food items on a backwoods activity or adventure. The Scout should indicate that they wish to do this requirement so that they can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I know about nature and what you are likely to see and experience as part of a backwoods activity.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will show an awareness of the environment they will explore and be able to state all the nature they are likely to experience in that area. List the wild things that could be seen in the area you are visiting. Explain how being in close contact with nature enables you to discover more.

competencies.statement: I can find directions by using star constellations and the sun/watch method.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show his/her knowledge in a practical way during daylight and nighttime settings. Basic directional indications are required (North, South, East, and West). The Scout should be comfortable with this knowledge and use it regularly when taking part in activities.

competencies.statement: I have attended at least one backwoods based overnight activity.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have attended at least two further backwoods activities – to those undertaken in previous levels). These activities can range from simple afternoon sessions to day long activities. At this level a scout should have camped out overnight in a shelter or ‘survival or backwoods adventure’ at least for one night.

competencies.statement: I know how to use and care for tools of all kinds safely.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to discuss best practice and how to care for the tools on camp. List the tools necessary for a backwoods adventure. Demonstrate how to use each tool safely. Demonstrate how to clean, care for and store tools when not in use.

competencies.statement: I know how to build a backwoods shelter using natural materials and how to return this material to nature.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to know when to build a shelter from natural materials rather than by using a plastic sheet and how to deconstruct the shelter after use. Natural shelters need a lot of covering to make a roof it is important that nature is not disturbed. The roof should be made of plastic sheeting and not ferns and leaves. Basic roof structure using materials found on the ground not cut down. Refer to the ‘ Leave No Trace’ principles.

competencies.statement: I know how to cook a variety of foods using different backwoods methods.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate how to cook a variety of food using a number of different methods, stick, broiler, foil, hot stones etc. Demonstrate the hot stone method of cooking. Fry an egg. Plank a fish. Make a camp twist. Cook a burger on a broiler.

competencies.statement: I know the safety considerations that are necessary before embarking on an activity or adventure.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will be aware of the possible dangers of the activity and what procedures to follow if an accident results. Use of tools. Care around fires. Food hygiene. Cooking food.

competencies.statement: I can make a length of cordage using naturally found fibers.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to produce a length of cord made of natural materials. This might be produced using nettle fibers, bark fibers, plant fibers and root fibers. The length of the cordage needs to be a minimum of 60cm in length.

competencies.statement: I can light a fire using flint and steel.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will be able to demonstrate how to light a fire using a flint and steel techniques resulting in the lighting of a fire.

competencies.statement: I can make myself comfortable on an overnight backwoods adventure using available natural materials.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain how with the use of minimal tools and expertise they can live successfully off the land. Woodsmanship needs to be second nature as a result of skill level. Be able to adapt to an environment quickly and with ease. Be able to build shelter to protect from elements. Be able to build a fire in any circumstances.

competencies.statement: I can carve a wooden spoon from a piece of wood.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to produce a wooden spoon and be able to discuss how it was made. The Scout can also demonstrate the making of a spoon under observation.

competencies.statement: I have attended at least two backwoods based activities.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have attended at least two further backwoods activities – to those undertaken in previous levels. At this level a Scout should have camped out overnight in a shelter.

competencies.statement: I know what Patrol and personal equipment is necessary for a successful adventure.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should indicate in list form the items they need to bring with them for a backwoods activity over a number of days. Show an indepth understanding of a backwoods environment and what tools are useful and necessary. Discuss the difference between backwoods and real survival situations. Demonstrate an understanding of woodland environments and what equipment can aid living in this environment. (General Info in Scouting Trail ‘Preparing for Adventure’, ‘Room Outside’, ‘Dining Out’ and ‘Backwoods Living’)

competencies.statement: I know all of the elements of the ‘Leave No Trace’ programme.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be aware that living and walking through open countryside has an impact of some kind and that we need to minimize this intrusion. The Scout should suggest best practice and discuss how to minimize impact while also enjoying the outdoor experience.

competencies.statement: I can identify edible fruits and berries that are found in nature.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to discuss the different fruits and berries that can be found in the local area. The Scout should be able to identify the edible and inedible berries in nature.

competencies.statement: I can prepare the foods I find in nature for cooking.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be confident and skilled, to such an extent, that they know how to find food in nature and the methods that can be used to prepare and cook it. There are many different methods and the Scout should be able to discuss and demonstrate the benefits and merits of various methods.

competencies.statement: I can find my way using natural direction indicators.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should discuss the different ways of identifying direction using nature indicators. The Scout should then be able to show how to find these indicators and point out a number of them to others.

competencies.statement: I can catch and prepare a fish for cooking.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to catch a fish. He/she can use whatever method they prefer. Once the fish is caught they should be able to prepare the fish for cooking and cook it. This is best done in a practical way on an activity.

competencies.statement: I have led at least one backwoods activity.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should have attended at least 2 further backwoods activities – to those undertaken in previous stages). At this stage a Scout should have camped out overnight in a shelter on a full backwoods style adventure.

competencies.statement: I know a number of ways of constructing shelters and bivvys.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to demonstrate with their Patrol over a number of activities their ability in regard to shelter building.

competencies.statement: I know the likely hazards that may be present in woodland or open countryside.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show an understanding of the backwoods environment and venue and discuss possible hazards that might present during the activity. Rough terrain, rodents, insects, water dangers, open fires.

competencies.statement: I know how to light and maintain a fire using fire by friction methods.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will demonstrate this skill and result in lighting a fire. Prepare a fire site. Gather the necessary tinder materials. Light a fire using flint and steel. Light a fire using a friction bow and drill.

competencies.statement: I know how to live in the country without disturbing the balance of nature in any way.
competencies.explanation: The Leave No Trace principles should be fully understood and demonstrated in practical situation on camp and at the break of camp. The Scout should lead the final check and clean up of a campsite on a number of occasions. Dispose of waste properly. Respect farm animals and wildlife. Minimise camping impact and the effects of fire. Be considerate of others. Travel and camp on durable surfaces. Leave what you find. Plan ahead and prepare.

competencies.statement: I know how to make utensils by carving and other methods.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to carve using a penknife or an axe - a number of utensils such as. A spoon , pot lifter , kebab stick, Scout stave.

competencies.statement: I can cook a meal without using common utensils.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to demonstrate this skill in a backwoods situation.

competencies.statement: I have led at least one overnight backwoods or survival based activity.
competencies.explanation: The Scout at this level should have a wide experience of taking part in backwoods and survival based adventures and activities. Their skill should be observed in action and practical situations on these activities. Taking part in overnight rather than day activities will enable the full extent of the Scouts skill and expertise to be observed and challenged.

competencies.statement: I know a number of ways of constructing shelters capable of being used for a number of nights.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show an ability to build shelters using any available materials (natural and man-made). The shelter should be able to accommodate at least two people in relative comfort and protection from the elements.

competencies.statement: I know how to prepare, cook and store food in backwoods conditions.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will be able to prepare and cook a variety of food. This needs to be demonstrated in a backwoods environment. Find natural food in your surroundings. Prepare this food alongside food brought to location. Make a food storage gadget from the materials that are available to you or suggest ways of storing food safely.

competencies.statement: I know the different edible foods that can be eaten safely in the wilds.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will have an indepth knowledge of wild foods, where they can be found, when they are in season and how they should be cooked correctly. Discuss the possible food that can be eaten. Identify these wild foods in a natural location. Show how they are prepared for eating.

competencies.statement: I hold a first aid cert (outdoor) or equivalent REC.
competencies.explanation: A Scout is expected to hold a first aid certificate if they are attempting this level of expertise in this adventure skill

competencies.statement: I know how to make a variety of tools, and useful gadgets to survive in nature over a period of time.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show an ability to make tools, gadgets and useful items using any available materials (natural and man-made). These items should have a purpose and be useful for living in nature. These items are best demonstrated in a practical situation.

competencies.statement: I can live comfortably in a number of different natural situations, with minimal equipment.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain how with the use of minimal tools and expertise they can live successfully of the land. Woodsmanship needs to be second nature as a result of skill level. Be able to adapt to an environment quickly and with ease. Be able to build shelter to protect from elements. Be able to build a fire in any circumstances.

competencies.statement: I have lead at least three backwoods adventures.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should have lead at least three backwoods adventures. These can be comprised of programme activities lasting an afternoon, day or weekend. The key feature of their involvement is leadership of the activity, passing on of skills to younger members and overseeing health and safety considerations particularly in relation to food gathering, preparation and cooking.

competencies.statement: I have participated in a survival weekend activity.
I have run at least two backwoods skills training sessions for my Scout Group/County
I have participated in a survival activity outside my usual Scouting environment.
I know what equipment is needed for making pioneering gadgets.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to list and explain the use of various pieces of equipment used in the construction of simple small pioneering projects; Poles and staves; Ropes and sisal for lashing;

competencies.statement: I know how to build a gadget using elastic band techniques.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should build a series of gadgets using elastic bands and bamboo poles. Pioneering structure techniques need to be observed in the building structure; Simple tripod frame; Patrol Flagpole; Pot stand

competencies.statement: I can be responsible for myself while we are pioneering.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to show an awareness of what is happening around himself/herself. The need for care and safety and awareness of others and what they are doing should be evident in their behavior.

competencies.statement: I understand why I should follow directions from an instructor.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know about the importance of listening to the instructor so that they are aware of what to do and the dangers of doing things that they don’t fully understand.

competencies.statement: I have built at least two simple pioneering gadgets.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should have participated in the construction of at least two simple pioneering gadgets perhaps constructed on a camping adventure or as part of a pioneering activity.

competencies.statement: I know how to get help if someone is hurt.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to show an ability to recognize that someone is hurt and needs help. The Scout should also know how to get help and by what means. How to recognize that someone is hurt. How to compare injured parts with uninjured parts. Methods of getting help. Methods of caring for someone that is hurt.

competencies.statement: I can tie the basic knots I need for pioneering.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to tie under supervision and use: clove hitch, reef knot, square lashing tripod lashing, diagonal and sheer lashings.

competencies.statement: I can prepare ropes for use in pioneering.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be observed doing or assisting others in selecting ropes for a pioneering project. ( Reference Scouting Trail Pages 178)

competencies.statement: I can coil a rope.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to coil a rope so it will not twist or curl. (Underarm coiling should not be encouraged as it causes the rope to twist and curl). The Scout should also be able to ‘finish’ off the end of the coil so it can be carried and stored.

competencies.statement: I can undertake tasks assigned to me while we are pioneering.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be observed in action over a number of a pioneering project.

competencies.statement: I have made a knot board.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will have made a simple knot board for his/her Lodge/Six/Patrol Corner. The knot board should display at least six basic knots of their choice.

competencies.statement: I have built at least three simple pioneering gadgets using elastic band techniques.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should have participated in the construction of at least three simple pioneering gadgets perhaps constructed on a camping adventure or as part of a pioneering activity. The Scout should be showing a progression of skills in the construction of these simple projects.

competencies.statement: I know what equipment I need for making various pioneering gadgets.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will explain how to choose a suitable project with the skills of the Patrol in mind and the key steps necessary to enable it to be built safely. Preparation and planning skills. Preparing an equipment list. Listing the main pioneering elements in a structure.

competencies.statement: I know how to treat basic cuts and scratches.
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to talk themselves through the process of treatment. This demonstration/talk can be done in a practical way on a volunteer. How to clean the wound. How to reassure the casualty. How to apply a bandage.

competencies.statement: I know about the safety precautions that are needed when pioneering.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know how a structure is built and discuss possible danger points and what to do to avoid accidents during an activity. The use of hard hats. How a heavy load might be lifted. How to use guy ropes for security. Discuss how a project is constructed. Be able to identify danger points in the build process.

competencies.statement: I am aware of the Leave No Trace principles.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should demonstrate an understanding of the key points in a practical way in a camp situation. Dispose of waste properly. Respect farm animals and wildlife. Minimise camping impact and the effects of fire. Be considerate of others. Travel and camp on durable surfaces. Leave what you find. Plan ahead and prepare.

competencies.statement: I have taught other scouts how to tie some basic knots.
competencies.explanation: This is best observed in actions during a pioneering activity. The Scout should be supportive and help the younger Scout become proficient at tying knots of all kinds.

competencies.statement: I have built at least two gadgets using ropes and poles.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should have participated in the construction of at least two simple pioneering gadgets perhaps constructed on a camping adventure or as part of a pioneering activity. The Scout should be showing a progression of skill in the construction of these simple projects.

competencies.statement: I know the correct use, care, and storage of the tools we use in pioneering.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to show an awareness of the tools likely to be used in pioneering activities, how these tools are used and cared for so that they are working properly. List the tools necessary for pioneering - saw, knife, mallet, spade, sledge hammer. Demonstrate how to use each tool safely. Demonstrate how to clean, care for and store tools when not in use.

competencies.statement: I know the different types of ropes used in pioneering.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to ‘size’ a rope and select the right ropes to use for different elements of a pioneering project. Know the difference between natural and synthetic rope.

competencies.statement: I know how to take care of ropes of all kinds.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to talk about ropes and demonstrate how to look for damage and care for ropes by not over straining. The Scout should be able to coil large ropes and prepare them for storage. Coil a rope. Know how to check rope for fraying, grit, over straining, friction burns. Discuss how to clean a rope. Demonstrate how to coil a heavy rope and tie it up for storage.

competencies.statement: I know how to tie the knots necessary for building rope and pole structures safely.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to demonstrate through the building of a structure all the pioneering knots and lashings, attachment of safety ropes and guys, how to tie off securely to an anchor. Clove hitch, round turn and two halve hitches, square, diagonal, sheer, tripod lashing, Norwegian lashing, figure of eight loop, sheet bend.

competencies.statement: I know the safety precautions to be observed for the safe lifting of pioneering spars.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to discuss the method used to lift a pioneering pole to a height and demonstrate the procedure during the construction of a project. Demonstrate how a sheer legs is constructed and used to aid lifting. Demonstrate how a single pole can be used for leverage with the aid of a rope. Discuss the arrangement and management of a lift. Care area and fall space of a structure.

competencies.statement: I can use guys to make a pioneering gadgets stable.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should show an understanding of why guys will be necessary and why the structure will need to be secured. The Scout should then set up guy ropes on a structure before it is raised and lead the securing of those guys using pegs or pickets.

competencies.statement: I can tie the main lashings necessary to make most pioneering gadgets.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will demonstrate that they can tie the proper lashing associated with a pioneering structure correctly.

competencies.statement: I know the basic components of pioneering structures and how to make them.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know the basic elements that are combined to make pioneering structures – ‘A frames’, ‘Trestles’, Tripods, H frames. The Scout should also be able to demonstrate on a pioneering structure or via drawing the components present in a structure. Lastly, the Scout should be able to construct the components and discuss the need for uniformity and stability in their construction.

competencies.statement: I can be responsible for myself while pioneering.
competencies.explanation: This requirement implies that a Scout has some experience and is aware of how they should act, be responsible for their actions while working on a pioneering project. This is best demonstrated in a pioneering situation where the Scouts can be observed in action.

competencies.statement: I have built gadgets on camp and assisted my ‘team’ in building a tower or bridge.
competencies.explanation: The Scout, as part of a team, will have been involved in the construction of a number of projects. The Scout will discuss the steps required to build a structure. (Medium size projects are considered to be structures: Bridge and towers that are of simple construction design and low level height (approx 3 metres high). They will be capable of being built by a Patrol without too much adult intervention.) Choose a project or design a project. Plan how it is to be build. Identify the pioneering elements in its construction. Manage the build and deconstruction of a project.

competencies.statement: I know how to select suitable poles and spars for a pioneering project.
I know how to select suitable poles and spars for a pioneering project.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be observed directing his/her Patrol in the selection of pioneering poles for a project. Demonstrate how to choose suitable poles. List the ropes, lengths and sizes, required for a project.

competencies.statement: I know how to treat cuts and sprains.
competencies.explanation: Scouts need to talk themselves through the process of treatment. This demonstration/talk can be done in a practical way on a volunteer. State the rules of First aid. Demonstrate how to treat a minor cut. Discuss how they would know a bone is broken. Discuss how they would take care of the victim. Discuss what they would tell a medical person when summoning help.

competencies.statement: I can help a younger Scout to build a pioneering gadget.
competencies.explanation: This is best observed in action during the construction of a pioneering project. The Scout should be supportive and help the younger Scout achieve his objective. The younger Scout may be doing this project as part of their pioneering badge requirement.

competencies.statement: I know what to do in case of an accident and how to be safety conscious.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to show an ability to recognize that someone is hurt and needs help. They must indicate care for the injured party before departure for help. They should also know how to get help and by what means. How to recognize that someone is hurt. How to compare injured parts with uninjured parts. Methods of getting help. Methods of caring for someone that is hurt.

competencies.statement: I know all about the ‘Leave No Trace’ principles.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be aware that living and walking through open countryside has an impact of some kind and that we need to minimize this intrusion. The Scout should suggest best practice and discuss how to minimize impact while also enjoying the outdoor experience. Of particular concern is disturbance of river bed. Cutting and pruning of overhead branches.

competencies.statement: I can set up a simple pulley system for lifting and tensioning ropes.
competencies.explanation: The Scout needs to be aware of the recommended pulley combinations suggested for a project and explain why this combination is used. The Scout should also be able to discuss how a project is built in a safe manner using pulleys to assist in lifting loads and assembling the various elements of a project.

competencies.statement: I can coil, whip and splice a rope.
competencies.explanation: The Scout will demonstrate this skill by making a personal length of rope whipped at one end and an eye spice created at the other.

competencies.statement: I am aware of the building process/ procedure while pioneering.
I have taken part in the construction of at least two pioneering projects.
competencies.explanation: The Scout, as part of a team, will have been involved in the construction of a number of projects. The Scout will discuss the steps required to build a structure. (Large scale projects are considered to be structures bridges and towers that have sizeable design elements and may require the use of pulleys for tensioned rope work. (approx 3 meters high). They will be capable of being built by a Patrol but will require adult help in lifting and pulling project into place ) Choose a project or design a project. Plan how it is to be built. Identify the pioneering elements in its construction. Manage the build and deconstruction of a project.

competencies.statement: I know how to plan and construct pioneering projects to be built within my Patrol.
I know how to plan and construct pioneering projects to be built within my Patrol.
competencies.explanation: The Scout, as part of a team, will have been involved in the construction of a number of projects. The Scout will discuss the steps required to build a structure. The Scout will have completed a number of projects with their patrol and be observed doing so. Choose a project or design a project. Plan how it is to be built.
