competencies.explanation: The Scout should know the emergency number 112 (or 999) and say what kind of help is needed (Garda/Police, lifeboat, ambulance, fire brigade).

competencies.statement: I know why it is important to stay with a capsized boat.
competencies.explanation: A capsized boat is easier to see in the water than a head and the hull will help you stay afloat.

competencies.statement: I understand why I should follow directions from an instructor.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should understand how to behave on a boat and that there may be safety reason why an instructor doesn’t have time to explain a direction in advance.

competencies.statement: I can show the limits of where I may go each time I go afloat for sailing.
competencies.explanation: A Scout should know that for safety reasons they should stay within a defined area. They should know how far they can go.

competencies.statement: I know basic Sailing Theory.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know basic terminology like; tack, gybe, no-go area, sail, sheet, tiller.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in two half-day sailing exercises afloat consisting of a minimum of two hours afloat.
competencies.explanation: A half day is at least two hours on or around the water.

competencies.statement: I can assist with the rigging and de-rigging of a vessel.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should help with the rigging and de-rigging of a vessel. This will help them; know how to do it themselves and to learn the value of looking after equipment.

competencies.statement: I can explain what impact I may have on local vegetation when launching and retrieving a sailing dinghy.
competencies.explanation: Use a slipway where possible, avoid launching in or near nesting sites and where vegetation will be trampled down and damaged.

competencies.statement: I have discussed “Weil’s disease” and the precautions necessary to take part in open water activities.
competencies.explanation: Avoiding stagnant water and canal banks, proper personal hygiene before and after going afloat and covering open wounds with a water-proof plaster.

competencies.statement: I can put on my own personal floatation device properly.
competencies.explanation: This should include securing all fastenings and using a crotch strap where it is fitted.

competencies.statement: I know why I should wear suitable footwear.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain that it offers better grip, warmth and protection from sharp protrusions as well as debris in the water.

competencies.statement: I know basic sailing skills including what to do in the event of a capsize.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate basic skills which help them control the boat. These skills should include; Tacking. Control boat speed by trimming. Making progress to a point upwind. Having gybed under control at least once. The Scout should know that when a boat capsizes that they should not panic and should stay with the boat until someone comes along to help them run a capsize drill.

competencies.statement: I know Sailing theory.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know some of the theory of; Tacking. Gybing. No-go area.

competencies.statement: I can make a recognised distress signal.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to make one of the signals described in the International Regulations for the Prevention of Collisions at Sea.

competencies.statement: I know how to raise the alarm if I see somebody in difficulty on the water.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know how to make a call to the emergency services and give clear information as to what was seen and where.

competencies.statement: I know what hypothermia is.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should have knowledge of the signs and symptoms of hypothermia and have an understanding of why it is a problem.

competencies.statement: I know basic collision avoidance.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to identify channels and fairways in their local boating waters and understand why other boats may not be able to avoid a scout in a sailing dinghy. The Scout should know some basic rules of the road at sea. Simple rules like these will help them not crash into stuff; Small boats should avoid areas used by large commercial vessels. All vessels should stay on the starboard side of any channel or fairway.

competencies.statement: I can conduct myself in a careful and safe way in a boat and around water.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate that they understand safe behaviour; Always wear a PFD. No running or horse-play around water. Follow the directions of an instructor promptly.

competencies.statement: I can get a weather forecast.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to get a local or national weather forecast suitable for outdoor activity.

competencies.statement: I can tie the following knots; round-turn-and-two-half-hitches, figure of eight, bowline.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to tie the named knots on request.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in at least four half-day sailing activities.
competencies.explanation: A half day is at least two hours on or around the water.

competencies.statement: I can assist with rigging and de-rigging, launch and recover.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should take a more prominent role in the rigging and de-rigging as well as helping with the launch and recovery.

competencies.statement: I can put on my personal flotation device and adjust it properly.
competencies.explanation: Many PFDs are adjustable. The Scout should be able to make appropriate adjustments in order that the PFD fits the Scout correctly.

competencies.statement: I know why wearing layers of clothing is a good idea.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain the benefit of a layered approach and identify clothing best suited as a base, mid or top layer.

competencies.statement: I know basic sailing techniques.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know basic sailing techniques like; Raising and lowering hydrofils. Be able to stop a boat. Steering a triangular course. How and when to move in the boat maintaining balance and trim. Trimming sails. Leave and return to a jetty.

competencies.statement: I know the basics of sailing theory.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should know basic terminology like: Sheet in-out. Luff-up. Bear away. Ready about. Lee-ho.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in a capsize drill.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should have been involved in a capsize drill and have been talked through the steps to prepare for it and right the boat. If the boat has no buoyancy the Scout should know what to do in staying together and waiting for help.

competencies.statement: I can get into a dinghy from the water in a safe way.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an appropriate technique for the type of craft in use. The Scout may enter over the transom or at the beam as appropriate.

competencies.statement: I know how to do CPR and place a victim in the recovery position.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to demonstrate an up-to-date CPR technique on a suitable mannequin and demonstrate how to put an adult or child in the recovery position (also known as the safe-airway position).

competencies.statement: I know that I should follow the instructions of the person in charge of the boat.
competencies.explanation: The Scout may be aware that the person in charge of the boat is more experienced/qualified then themselves and following the instructions of this person ensures their safety on the water.

competencies.statement: I understand the terms used in a maritime weather forecast.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain the following terms and what they mean in the context of a maritime weather forecast; small craft warning, gale warning, imminent, soon, later.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in at least three full day sailing activities.
competencies.explanation: A full day afloat shall involve not less than five hours in or around a boat. This may include a lunch break. The scout will not be expected to be helming all the time.

competencies.statement: I can assist in launching, rigging and recovering a small sailing dinghy.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to demonstrate: How to secure a boat to a trolley and safely move it around ashore. Position the boat heat-to-wind. Identify the main parts of the boat, its rigging and sails. Assist with rigging the boat. With assistance launch and sail away from shore, sail back and recover the boat.

competencies.statement: I know the main principles of “Leave No Trace”.
competencies.explanation: Scouts should demonstrate an understanding of the key points in a practical way in a camp situation. Dispose of waste properly. Respect farm animals and wildlife. Minimise camping impact and the effects of fire. Be considerate of others. Travel and camp on durable surfaces. Leave what you find. Plan ahead and prepare.

competencies.statement: I know that there are different types of personal flotation device and know when and where each should be used.
competencies.explanation: The Scouting Ireland Boating Guidelines recommend different standards of PFD (50N, 100N, 150N, 275N) for use in different circumstances.

competencies.statement: I can explain why wearing the correct outerwear is important.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain that outerwear protects from both getting wet in rain and from the effects of wind-chill.

competencies.statement: I can paddle or row a boat in a straight line.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate their ability to propel a sailing dinghy with a paddle or suitable oars.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate all points of sailing with assistance as both crew and helm.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate their ability to sail, as helm and crew, demonstrating directional control, sail trim and balance while sailing on a; Beat. Beam reach. Broad Reach. Run.

competencies.statement: I can help another person safely into a sailing dinghy from the water.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to approach the casualty in the water and, by using a combination of lifting and moving their own body weight, assist another person in to a sailing dinghy from the water.

competencies.statement: I know sailing theory.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to; Describe the different points of sailing. Take correct action when boats on different tacks meet. Identify and use common sailing terms.

competencies.statement: I can coil a line and heave it to a casualty to affect a simulated rescue.
competencies.explanation: This should be done with a suitable weighted, floating line over a distance of at least 10m, bringing the casualty safely to shore.

competencies.statement: I know the safety precautions required for water based activities.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain Weather, Area, Tides, Clothing, Hull, Inventory, Tell Someone.

competencies.statement: I can describe the implications of offshore and onshore winds, high winds and no winds when sailing.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an awareness of onshore and offshore winds and how they impact on launching, recovery and safety. The Scout should also be able to explain the difficulties that too much or too little wind can cause for a sailing dinghy.

competencies.statement: I can describe how often high and low tides take place, and the implications these might when going afloat.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain the impact of the tide on the local boating waters. Such concerns as strong tidal flow and inaccessible moorings are relevant here.

competencies.statement: I know that where I may go boating may change in different conditions.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should understand that different areas may be safer in different wind directions and strengths.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in six full-day exercises afloat.
competencies.explanation: A full day could involve a journey such as on a river or lake, for example during a summer camp.

competencies.statement: I can rig and equip a sailing boat for safe use in a variety of weather conditions.
competencies.explanation: In demonstrating this the Scout should; Identify all the parts of the boat, rigging and sails. Rig the boat appropriately for the weather including demonstrating an ability to reef the sails while ashore. De-rig the boat after use and demonstrate proper care for the hull, sails and foils. Ensure that the boat is appropriately equipped with bailers, fenders, paddles/oars, painters etc.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate how to manoeuvre a sailing boat as a member of the crew.
competencies.explanation: As both crew and helm in light winds the Scout should demonstrate; Leaving and returning to a beach or slipway in the prevailing wind direction. Sailing on all points of the wind. Coming alongside a boat, pier or pontoon which is head to wind. Coming alongside a boat, pier or pontoon which is not head to wind. Recovering a man-over-board. heaving to. Sailing under jib only.

competencies.statement: I know the five essentials and can apply them to all points of sailing.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to demonstrate an ability to use course, trim, balance, sail trim and centreboard position to keep the boat sailing efficiently.

competencies.statement: I can take a leading role in mooring and unmooring a sailing boat including sailing on and off the mooring.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to direct a crew to safely pick up and cast off a mooring.

competencies.statement: I can assist in the anchoring of a sailing boat.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be capable of setting up the anchor, ensuring it is secured to the boat and deploying it overboard as directed by the helm.

competencies.statement: I can identify and name the main parts of common anchor types.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to name the principle parts of a Fisherman or Admiralty anchor, a Ploughshare style anchor and a Fluke style anchor.

competencies.statement: I know why it is important to have some training in first aid and can show how to care for someone who is very cold.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain the importance of having first aid training and demonstrate an ability to treat a casualty showing signs of hypothermia. It is desirable that a scout have some formal training in first aid.

competencies.statement: I know the parts of the International Regulations for the Prevention of Collisions at Sea that apply to my boat and local boating waters.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain which is the stand on vessel and which is the give way vessel in situations involving overtaking, crossing tracks and head on situations between two sailing boats and between motor boats and sailing boats. The Scout should also be able to explain correct procedure in and around channels and fairways.

competencies.statement: I can obtain a weather forecast and know how the information might affects planned activities afloat.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to obtain a suitable, up to date marine weather forecast for the relevant area and interpret how that forecast might alter plans.

competencies.statement: I know how currents and the ebb and flow of the tide affect my local boating waters.
I know the use of Channel 16 on marine VHF and have an understanding of the use of distress flares.
I have taken part in six full-day exercises afloat.
I have taken part in one expedition afloat.
competencies.explanation: An expedition is an extended journey afloat involving either camping ashore or sleeping aboard. The inland waterways of Ireland offer many opportunities for such expeditions.

competencies.statement: I can rig, de-rig, secure and care for the hull of the sailing boat that I use including using the listed control lines to set the boat up to sail efficiently upwind, downwind and on a reach demonstrating optimum sheeting.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be demonstrate rigging the boat for different circumstances using; Telltales. Jib sheeting angles. Halyard tension. Outhaul. Cunningham/downhaul. Kicker. Main sheet traveler.

competencies.statement: I can carry out the routine inspection of a personal flotation device.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate how to inspect a PFD for visual flaws such as tears, failed stitching, defective fastenings.

competencies.statement: I can take the helm of a sailing boat and demonstrate how to undertake various manoueveres.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate all the manoeuvres previously demonstrated in stronger winds than before, maintaining optimum sheeting most of the time. The Scout should demonstrate a basic roll-tack in light winds. The Scout should be able to explain the principles of sailing without a rudder and demonstrate sailing a beam reach without a rudder. The Scout should demonstrate an ability to sail backwards for a short distance.

competencies.statement: I know how to obtain maximum leverage when hiking or trapezing.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate hiking or trapezing technique.

competencies.statement: I know how sails and foils work and interact to drive a sailing boat.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain how sails produce thrust and how the hydrofoils counteract lateral movement to produce forward drive.

competencies.statement: I can take a leading part in anchoring a sailing boat including knowing how and when to use a tripping line.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to direct another Scout in ensuring the anchor is correctly set up, that the line is secured to the boat and not fouled and that they are anchoring in a suitable place. The Scout should explain the use of a tripping line.

competencies.statement: I know what to do if someone is caught under an inverted boat and can right an inverted boat.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate best practice in the event of a capsize beginning with a head-count to identify if a crew member is missing. The Scout should be able to explain the most likely reasons for entrapment (entanglement in sheets, hiking straps etc.) and how best to recover the casualty. The Scout should demonstrate an ability to take a leading role in recovering an inverted boat.

competencies.statement: I know what causes tides and how spring and neap tides might affect sailors.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain the interaction of the sun and moon and explain the increase in both tidal range and tidal rate during spring tides.

competencies.statement: I can recognise the main weather patterns illustrated by a synoptic chart and can interpret the forecast.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to look at a synoptic weather chart and use it to make their own weather forecast. For a given verbal weather forecast they should be able to interpret the terms used and describe the weather to be expected especially in terms of wind speed and direction and visibility.

competencies.statement: I can identify common weather conditions and describe how they may affect boating activities.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to describe the main weather features to expect with high or low pressure and with warm and cold fronts.

competencies.statement: I am familiar with the main features of restricted waters as defined for my group.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to describe the extent of Restricted Waters as defined for their group and identify headlands and any ports of refuge that might exist.

competencies.statement: I know how and when to make Distress and Urgency calls and Safety Announcements on Marine VHF.
I have taken part in eight full-day exercises afloat.
I have taken part in one expedition afloat.
I have instructed at least four people in four of the areas up to stage 3.
I can take a leading part in the manual handling of a sailing boat ashore ensuring safe handling procedures including preparing a sailing boat for safe transportation by road.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to direct a group of scouts handling a rowing boat ashore. The boat may be on a trailer or trolley or it may be carried. The Scout should show an awareness of potential risk to the boat, the scouts and members of the public who may be in the area. The scout should be able to direct others in putting the boat on the trailer and securing it with rope or straps. Ultimately responsibility for trailer suitability and load security must still lie with the driver of the towing vehicle.

competencies.statement: I can rig any sailing boat and identify all of the parts.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate a sufficient knowledge of the theory and practice of sailing that when presented with an unfamiliar sailing craft that they be able to rig it correctly.

competencies.statement: I know under which circumstances different personal flotation devices are appropriate.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain where and when the Scouting Ireland Boating Guidelines advise the use of different types of PFD.

competencies.statement: I can take charge of a sailing boat in moderate winds and carry out all the required manoeuvres including holding a course using instruments and transits.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to take charge of a boat and its crew to carry out all the manoeuvres previously required. This should be done on moderate wind conditions. The Scout should also demonstrate an ability to steer a course using either a compass or other electronic aid and also using suitable transits. The Scout should demonstrate an ability to reef while afloat and underway.

competencies.statement: I can take a leading part in selecting a good anchorage.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to select a suitable anchorage given due regard to sea bed, scope, shelter and sea.

competencies.statement: I can take charge of a boat and respond efficiently to a (simulated) emergency.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to explain and demonstrate an appropriate response to an emergency such as; MOB. Towing. Running repairs. Jury rig. The Scout should also be able to demonstrate how to shelter aboard a sailing boat while waiting for assistance.

competencies.statement: I know what lights should be shown by the most common vessels in my area and know what lights should be shown by a sailing boat.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to identify from sight or pictures, the nature of a vessel showing particular lights and describe what the vessel is doing. (crossing, head-on, overtaking...) The Scout should also be able to describe what lights are required on a rowing boat according to the International Regulations for the Prevention of Collisions at Sea.

competencies.statement: I know the International regulations for the Prevention of Collisions at Sea.
I can interpret the current forecast and make sound decisions on planned activities in view of expected weather and sea conditions and tidal effects.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate their ability to use weather forecasting information in planning activities afloat including knowing when to cancel an activity.

competencies.statement: I know the hazards and how the weather may affect “Restricted Waters” for my group.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to describe hazards such as rocks, tidal races, shipping lanes and overfalls which may exist in Restricted Waters as defined for their group. The Scout should also be able to describe how different wind directions may affect the area. Onshore and offshore winds may be of particular importance here.

competencies.statement: I know how to get suitable information for “Safe Enclosed” boating waters that are not my groups local waters (e.g. for camp).
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to identify suitable people to ask for information such as lifeboat crew, Fishermen and the coast guard and know what type of information they need to get.

competencies.statement: I can assist in developing a passage plan for day trips.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should be able to help others to make a plan bearing in mind wind, tides and currents, the ability of the crew, the nature of the craft and availability of rescue cover and suitable stopping places. Lights, landmarks and hazards along the route would be considered an essential part of the plan.

competencies.statement: I know how to read and set a chart, plot and estimate positions.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to use maritime charts and demonstrate an understanding of position marking conventions.

competencies.statement: I have a working knowledge of GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress Safety Systems) as it applies to EPIRBs (Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacons) and DSC (Digital Selective Calling).
I have taken part in ten full-day exercises afloat.
I have taken part in one overnight expedition afloat outside my normal boating waters.
I have instructed at least four people in at least six of the areas up to stage 5.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should choose six of the twelve topics listed for Stage 5 of the Rowing Adventure skills and instruct them to the required standard.

competencies.statement: I can take a leading part in the safe handling of sailing boat ashore.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to direct others in all areas of handling sailing boats ashore. The Scout should demonstrate due caution for the scouts doing the lifting as well as the boat and surrounding property.

competencies.statement: I can rig any sailing boat including optimizing the rig and boat for a given set of conditions.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate their ability to use all available adjustments to tune the rig for any particular set of conditions. The adjustments should include the following; Mast rake. Rig tension. Spreader length and angle. Mast ram/chocks.

competencies.statement: I understand the different safety precautions that must be taken when a group of boats is operating together.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an understanding of the different problems that can arise with multi-craft activities. This might include differences in performance or crew ability and the additional communications requirements to ensure boats do not become too far separated.

competencies.statement: I can carry out all the sailing manoeuvres in strong winds including setting up and controlling the boat while on the plane.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate a range of activities designed to develop and practice specific aspects of boat handling and boat speed including; an ability to carry out an effective roll-tack in all wind strengths. a knowledge of how and when to shorten sail including dropping one sail or another as necessary. maximising boat speed in waves. optimum course to steer. holding position. Heaving-to.

competencies.statement: I can describe how sails interact and demonstrate techniques to maximise this effect.
I have a good understanding of the merits of different anchor types for different locations and conditions.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should explain the merits of different types of anchor in different circumstances and identify the type of anchor best suited to local waters. This may require identifying more than one type of anchor if different seabed conditions exist in various parts of the groups Day Cruising waters.

competencies.statement: I can carry our MOB and capsize drills in test conditions.
I know what sound signals the most common types of vessel in my area should make.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate knowledge of the various sound signals (fog signals and general sound signals for manoeuvring) that may be used by the types of vessel the Scout is likely to encounter in the Groups Day Cruising Waters.

competencies.statement: I have researched at least five pieces of weather lore.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate knowledge of at least five pieces of weather lore (Red sky at night..., spiders spinning webs...). Their knowledge should include an evaluation as to how useful any piece of weather lore might be in predicting the local weather.

competencies.statement: I am familiar with ‘Day Cruising Waters’ for my group.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate knowledge of the extent of Day Cruising Waters for their group and the various features of it including, but not limited to; ports of refuge, man-made and natural hazards, shipping lanes and channels.

competencies.statement: I can use the information from a charts etc. to plan an expedition in restricted waters.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should use information from published and informal sources to produce an expedition plan. This plan would include launch and recovery sites, camp sites, sources of fresh water and supplies, tidal streams and ranges, ports of refuge, emergency plans, inventory lists etc. At this stage a scout might consider obtaining the ISA Small Boat Navigation Certificate or equivalent.

competencies.statement: I have an understanding of the ‘capture effect’ as it applies to marine VHF.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should explain their understanding of the Capture effect and how it may impact on communications.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate the rope work required for this stage.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate the previous knots in use as well as demonstrating a short splice, jury-rig knot, double sheet-bend in use.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in ten full-day exercises afloat.
I have taken part in one overnight expedition involving more than one boat.
I have instructed at least four people in at least seven of the areas up to stage 6.
I can rig any sailing boat and identify all the parts.
I can carry out all the sailing manoeuvres required for this stage to a very high standard.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to carry out all the manoeuvres previously mentioned to a very high standard including demonstrating constant attention to the five essentials.

competencies.statement: I can use an outboard engine to manoeuvre a boat while in displacement mode.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to manoeuvre a sailing boat propelled by an outboard or inboard motor.

competencies.statement: I have the skills and knowledge required to spend a night on board or camping.
competencies.explanation: Depending on the nature of vessel available the scout may chose to overnight aboard (underway or not) or camp in a suitable location ashore.

competencies.statement: I can anchor a boat efficiently to two anchors.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to lay a boat to two anchors either for added security or to reduce scope.

competencies.statement: I can jury-rig a sailing boat, improvise and deploy a sea anchor and know what spares and tools should be carried aboard.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should explain what spares and tools should be carried aboard in safe enclose, restricted or day cruising waters. The Scout should also demonstrate an ability to improvise a sea-anchor from materials which could be expected aboard a sailing boat. The Scout should explain when and why to use a sea-anchor. The Scout should demonstrate an ability to Jury-rig a sailing boat while under way demonstrating an understanding of sail balance and the forces which may be applied to strong-points etc.

competencies.statement: I have completed the requirement for the Emergencies Skills Stage 7.
I know how to interact with the emergency services.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate knowledge of how to communicate with the emergency services using both communications technology and visual signals. The Scout should demonstrate an understanding of what information the emergency services might need in an emergency situation.

competencies.statement: I know what sound signals the most common types of vessel in my area should make.
I can identify the type, aspect and behaviour of vessels by day or night from lights, shapes and sounds.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate their knowledge of lights, day shapes and sounds and what information they give regarding the vessel.

competencies.statement: I know the procedure for entry to and departure from a harbour and understand the requirement to file a passage plan under SOLAS regulations.

I can complete a rough synoptic chart from a maritime weather forecast or similar data and use this information to make sound decisions on planned activities in view of expected weather and sea conditions.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate an ability to construct an approximate synoptic chart from the data given in the wide area shipping forecast broadcast by the BBC. This chart should give the approximate position of any cyclones and anti-cyclones as well as any weather fronts.

competencies.statement: I am familiar with any local rules and bylaws that apply to Day Cruising Waters for my group.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate their knowledge of any rules any bylaws concerning boating in Day Cruising Waters. This may include areas of restricted activity, speed limits, restrictions on times of operation and craft given stand-on privilege, among others.

competencies.statement: I can devise a pilot/passage plan and programme that plan into a GPS.
I can demonstrate the rope work required for this stage.
competencies.explanation: The Scout should demonstrate the previous knots in use as well as demonstrating the Bowline-on-the-bight and sheep shank.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in ten full-day exercises afloat.
I have taken part in an overnight expedition in coastal waters.
I have instructed at least four people in at least five of the areas up to stage 8.

skills.name: UK Scout - Digital Citizen
skills.preface: UK Scout Staged Activity Badge - Digital citizenship, online safety, and responsible technology use. Supported by Nominet.

competencies.statement: I can map out my regular digital actions and discuss my digital footprint
competencies.explanation: In a creative way of your choice, map out regular digital actions such as searches, clicks or posts. Discuss with other young people the information you leave behind as a result of these digital actions, and whether that's OK or not.

competencies.statement: I can create a secure password with a trusted adult
competencies.explanation: Learn how to create a secure password and make one of your own. Always do this with a trusted adult to ensure it's done safely.

competencies.statement: I know how to respond positively to unkind behaviour online
competencies.explanation: Share three ways young people can respond positively when someone's being unkind or dishonest, including telling an adult if someone's making you feel uncomfortable.

competencies.statement: I can use online services to learn a new skill
competencies.explanation: Use an online service to learn a new skill and show others what you've learnt. This develops digital literacy and research skills.

competencies.statement: I can create a list of online rights for young people
competencies.explanation: Create a list of rights that you think you should have as a young person when online. Find online examples of where you think these rights are respected.

competencies.statement: I can track and reflect on my time spent online
competencies.explanation: For a week, keep track of how much time you spend online and what you're doing. Looking back over the week, discuss with someone if you're happy with how you spent your time or not.

competencies.statement: I can distinguish between facts and opinions online
competencies.explanation: Show that you can spot the difference between facts and opinions posted online. This develops critical thinking and media literacy skills.

competencies.statement: I can investigate how people from different backgrounds interact online
competencies.explanation: Investigate how people from different backgrounds interact online. Share how you'd act differently because of these differences. People might be from different countries, be different ages, have different abilities or amounts of money, etc.

competencies.statement: I can share learning using both online and offline tools
competencies.explanation: In a team, learn about a topic you care about and share with others what you've learnt. You must use a mixture of online and offline tools, and discuss which you preferred and why.

competencies.statement: I can map out how others' digital actions affect my privacy
competencies.explanation: In a creative way of your choice, map out what digital actions other people take which makes information about you public. Discuss with other young people what the positive and negative consequences of this might be, and what actions you can take to protect yourself.

competencies.statement: I can help others know what to do if uncomfortable online
competencies.explanation: Create something that helps other young people to know what they should do if they're made to feel uncomfortable online, and where they can find support.

competencies.statement: I can analyze my online network diversity
competencies.explanation: Investigate if the people you interact with most online are similar to you, or different to you (ie what are their ages, genders, ethnicities, hobbies etc?). What impact might that have on the views and opinions you see and believe?

competencies.statement: I can use online services to research personal opportunities
competencies.explanation: Use several online services to research a personal opportunity that excites you but you know little about (such as a new hobby, studying at college or university, or a specific career).

competencies.statement: I can collaborate digitally to benefit my community
competencies.explanation: In a team, use a digital collaboration tool of your choice to achieve one of the following: Something that benefits your Scout Group, Something that benefits a local charity, Something that promotes young people's voices to local decision makers.

competencies.statement: I understand my rights regarding online information
competencies.explanation: Show that you understand your rights regarding online information by completing one of the following: In a creative way of your choice, show all the information someone could find about you online and how you'd hide that information if you wanted to, OR Research different ways in which your personal information can be used by algorithms or targeted advertising, and create an activity to show other young people what you found out.

competencies.statement: I can debate topics using online evidence
competencies.explanation: Take part in a debate on a topic that you think there may be lots of misinformation about online. Use evidence you've found online only. After the debate, discuss how easy it was to know if the evidence you found was reliable or not.

competencies.statement: I can create a digital version of the Scout Law
competencies.explanation: Create a digital version of the Scout Law which shows how each law can be followed when online.

competencies.statement: I can complete and share online learning
competencies.explanation: Complete an online training course of your choice and share some of what you learned with other young people.

competencies.statement: I can collaborate digitally with an international team
competencies.explanation: In a team that includes young people from other parts of the country or world, use a digital collaboration tool of your choice to achieve one of the following: Something that benefits Scouts, Something that benefits a charity or cause you all care about, Something that promotes young people's voices within national decision makers.

skills.name: UK Scout - Digital Maker
skills.preface: UK Scout Staged Activity Badge - Digital making, coding, and creative technology skills. Supported by Raspberry Pi.

competencies.statement: I know what a computer is and understand uses for digital technology
competencies.explanation: Show that you know what a computer is and understand that there are lots of uses for digital technology in everyday life. Think about where you see computer systems and technology in your day-to-day life, and about how digital technology helps make things better or easier.

competencies.statement: I can create graphics for digital projects
competencies.explanation: Create a graphic for a computer game, app, or website. This could be a background scene, character, or other image.

competencies.statement: I can write clear instructions for computers
competencies.explanation: Write clear instructions for a computer or person to follow to complete a task. This develops computational thinking and algorithm design skills.

competencies.statement: I can create interactive or animated digital art
competencies.explanation: Create a piece of interactive or animated digital art using software. This could be done using Scratch, Python, or other creative coding tools.

competencies.statement: I can create a simple computer program for scouting
competencies.explanation: Create a simple computer program to help with a scouting activity, and try it out. This could be a game, quiz, or utility tool.

competencies.statement: I can make a digital creation that interacts with the world
competencies.explanation: Make a simple digital creation that uses code to interact with the wider world through inputs (such as buttons or typing on a keyboard) and outputs (such as a computer screen, sound, or lights).

competencies.statement: I can create a digital project with multiple features
competencies.explanation: Create a digital project that combines at least two different skills, such as programming, digital art, or user interaction. The project should have a clear purpose and be tested to ensure it works as intended.

competencies.statement: I can share and explain my digital project
competencies.explanation: Demonstrate your digital project to others and explain how you created it, what tools you used, and how it could be improved or extended.

competencies.statement: I can help others with digital making
competencies.explanation: Help another Scout or group of Scouts with a digital making project. This could involve debugging code, suggesting improvements, or teaching them how to use a tool or technique.

competencies.statement: I can combine digital skills to solve scouting challenges
competencies.explanation: Using a combination of programming, digital art, digital devices, electronic components, and other appropriate materials, create something that could serve a purpose in a Scouting activity. This should demonstrate integration of multiple digital making skills.

competencies.statement: I can participate in digital making events or mentor others
competencies.explanation: Attend a digital making event and show your work, or help somebody else in your section or another section to work towards a Digital Maker Staged Activity badge. You could take part in a Raspberry Jam, attend a Code Club, attend a hackathon, or visit a Coderdojo.

competencies.statement: I can solve real-world problems with digital making
competencies.explanation: Identify a real-life local or global problem and design, build, test, and improve a solution by combining your digital making skills and selecting appropriate software tools, digital devices, components, and materials. This should demonstrate advanced problem-solving and technical skills.

competencies.statement: I can document and share my project for others to replicate
competencies.explanation: Create and share a resource that would allow someone else to replicate your project with minimal previous knowledge. This resource should be digital, and it can be any format you like: a video (or a series!), an online (printable) document, an entry on a tutorials website such as Instructables, a blog post. Alternatively, meet with people who could benefit from your solution to share how you created it and explain how it can help them.

skills.name: UK Scout - Musician
skills.preface: UK Scout Staged Activity Badge - Developing musical skills through performance, knowledge and appreciation of music

competencies.statement: I can listen to and sing back a short tune
competencies.explanation: Listen to a short tune of a couple of lines and then sing it back, demonstrating musical memory and pitch recognition.

competencies.statement: I can listen to and clap out the rhythm of a tune
competencies.explanation: Listen to another tune and then beat or clap out the rhythm, showing ability to identify and reproduce rhythmic patterns.

competencies.statement: I can sing or play two different types of song or tune in front of others
competencies.explanation: Sing or play two different types of song or tune on your chosen instrument – remember your voice is an instrument too. You must perform in front of other people, either in Scouting or at a public performance such as a group show or school concert.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate musical exercises I use to practice
competencies.explanation: Demonstrate some of the musical exercises that you use to practice your skills, showing understanding of technique development.

competencies.statement: I can talk about my instrument or singing and why I enjoy it
competencies.explanation: Talk about your instrument and why you enjoy playing it. Alternatively, you could talk about the songs you sing and why you enjoy singing them.

competencies.statement: I can talk about the music I most like to listen to
competencies.explanation: Tell your assessor about the music that you most like to listen to, demonstrating music appreciation and personal engagement.

competencies.statement: I have reached Grade One standard for musical performance
competencies.explanation: Reach Grade One standard for the Associated Board of the Royal School of Music (or similar). It can be on an instrument of your choice or by singing.

competencies.statement: I can perform two different types of song or tune in front of others
competencies.explanation: Sing or play two different types of song or tune on your chosen instrument. You must perform in front of other people either in Scouting or at a public performance.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate the musical exercises I use to practice
competencies.explanation: Demonstrate some of the musical exercises that you use to practice your skills, showing understanding of technique development and regular practice routines.

competencies.statement: I can talk about my instrument or singing and why I enjoy it
competencies.explanation: Talk about your instrument and why you enjoy playing it, or talk about the songs you sing and why you enjoy singing them.

competencies.statement: I can name a piece of music associated with my instrument
competencies.explanation: Name a piece of music associated with your instrument, showing knowledge of repertoire for your chosen instrument.

competencies.statement: I can name several musicians I have heard
competencies.explanation: Name several musicians who you have heard, demonstrating awareness of performers and musical artists.

competencies.statement: I can talk about my musical interests and compare music I listen to with music I play
competencies.explanation: Talk about your own interests in music, including what you listen to most and how it's similar or different to the music you play or sing.

competencies.statement: I have reached Grade Two standard for musical performance
competencies.explanation: Reach Grade Two standard for the Associated Board of the Royal School of Music (or similar). It can be on an instrument of your choice or by singing.

competencies.statement: I can perform two different types of song or tune as a solo or with others
competencies.explanation: Sing or play, as a solo or with others, two different types of song or tune on your chosen instrument. You must perform in front of other people, either in Scouting or at a public performance such as a group show or school concert.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate musical exercises I use to practice
competencies.explanation: Demonstrate some of the musical exercises that you use to practice your skills, showing understanding of technique development and regular practice routines.

competencies.statement: I can talk about my instrument or singing and why I enjoy it
competencies.explanation: Talk about your instrument and why you enjoy playing it, or talk about the songs you sing and why you enjoy singing them.

competencies.statement: I can talk about three well-known pieces of music associated with my instrument
competencies.explanation: Talk about three well known pieces of music or songs associated with your instrument, showing knowledge of repertoire and musical context.

competencies.statement: I can discuss my musical interests and how they relate to my performance
competencies.explanation: Talk about your own interests in music, including what you listen to most and how this is similar to or different from the music you play or sing.

competencies.statement: I have reached Grade Three standard for musical performance
competencies.explanation: Reach Grade Three standard for the Associated Board of the Royal School of Music (or similar). It can be on an instrument of your choice or by singing.

competencies.statement: I can perform three different types of song or tune including one solo and one with other musicians
competencies.explanation: Sing or play three different types of song or tune on your chosen instrument. One should be a solo and one should be played with other musicians in an arrangement of your choice. Your performance should be public, such as at a Group show, school concert or church service.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate the musical exercises I use to practice
competencies.explanation: Demonstrate some of the musical exercises that you use to practice your skills, showing understanding of technique development.

competencies.statement: I can talk about my instrument or singing and why I enjoy it
competencies.explanation: Talk about your instrument and why you enjoy playing it, or talk about the songs you sing and why you enjoy singing them.

competencies.statement: I can discuss my musical interests and how they relate to my performance
competencies.explanation: Talk about your own interests in music, including what you listen to most and how it's similar or different to the music you play or sing.

competencies.statement: I have reached Grade Five standard for musical performance
competencies.explanation: Reach Grade Five standard for the Associated Board of the Royal School of Music (or similar) on the instrument of your choice or by singing.

competencies.statement: I can perform three different types of song or tune including one solo and one with other musicians
competencies.explanation: Sing or play three different types of song or tune on your chosen instrument. One should be a solo and one should be played with other musicians in an arrangement of your choice. Your performance should be public such as at a group show or church service.

competencies.statement: I can demonstrate the musical exercises I use to practice
competencies.explanation: Demonstrate some of the musical exercises that you use to practice your skills, showing advanced understanding of technique development.

competencies.statement: I can talk about my instrument or singing and why I enjoy it
competencies.explanation: Talk about your instrument and why you enjoy playing it, or talk about the songs you sing and why you enjoy singing them.

competencies.statement: I can name several well-known pieces of music associated with my instrument
competencies.explanation: Name several well known pieces of music associated with your instrument, demonstrating knowledge of the repertoire and musical tradition.

competencies.statement: I can name several musicians associated with my instrument
competencies.explanation: Name several musicians associated with your instrument, showing awareness of performers and interpreters of your instrument's repertoire.

competencies.statement: I can discuss my musical interests and how they relate to my performance
competencies.explanation: Talk about your own interests in music, including what you listen to most and how it's similar or different to the music you play or sing.

competencies.statement: I can name at least 4 things that I know use radio waves
competencies.explanation: e.g. Mobile phones, TV, Radio, WiFi, walkie talkie, Satellites, GPS, Bluetooth, Radar

competencies.statement: I know my parents/guardian/ICE contact phone number and can dial it on a mobile phone
I can name some radio stations I can hear from my home/den/car
I know the difference between Commercial and Amateur radio
I know why amateur radio is a licensed hobby
I know what morse code is
I know some aspects of Amateur radio language
competencies.explanation: Phonetic Alphabet and Q codes, callsigns. I know what a callsign is and the prefix of my own country and I can spell my name using the phonetic alphabet.

competencies.statement: I can use a walkie talkie
I know what a circuit and EMF is and observed how a circuit affects a compass
I have built a simple circuit
competencies.explanation: e.g. Artibot-scribble robot, morse key, fan.

competencies.statement: I know where Sound, Radio and Light frequencies are with regard to the Spectrum of Electro Magnetic Frequencies
I know the main components of an amateur radio radio system
competencies.explanation: Antenna, receiver, speaker, microphone, transmitter.

competencies.statement: I know what short wave listening is and I have tuned in to and can recognise morse code, data and voice signals
I know what the RST system for signal reporting is
I know how to look up a callsign of an amateur radio station on qrz.com
I have listened to and logged 5 QSO’s and have identified the operators country
I have operated an amateur or marine radio and given my name and station callsign using the phonetic alphabet
competencies.explanation: Spoken on the radio to another operator.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in JOAT-JOTI
I understand low frequency, high frequency, HF, VHF & UHF and can name some characteristics
I understand low frequencies need larger antennas and high frequencies need smaller antennas
I understand the concept of signal-to-noise ratio and how directional antennas help
I understand and can explain the 3 modes of propagation
competencies.explanation: Free-space, Groundwave & Ionospheric prorogation.

competencies.statement: I can explain why I can hear distant stations on MW, LW and SW
competencies.explanation: How these changes from night and day.

competencies.statement: I know how space weather, particularly the Sun affects radio wave propagation
I know what objects in the Solar System emit radio waves and I understand the concept of signal to noise ratio
I understand how a repeater and DMR works and I have made a QSO via a repeater or DMR
I understand the main radio controls and how to use them
competencies.explanation: VFO A/B, AGC, RF gain, AF gain, Band select, Mode select, Tune.

competencies.statement: I have decoded an SSTV signal
I have a log of 25 shortwave/HF stations that I have heard on the radio
competencies.explanation: Can include Amateur and Commercial Stations. Log must include time, date, frequency, mode and signal report, at least 10 of the logs must be in daylight hours and 10 in night time hours.

competencies.statement: I can explain the function of following basic electronic components
competencies.explanation: Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, Transistor, Diode/LED. I have completed a working circuit using at least three of these components.

competencies.statement: I have taken part in a scouting event and talked to another operator on the radio
competencies.explanation: Giving my station callsign.

competencies.statement: I can explain resonance and the basics of tuning a half-wave dipole antenna
I can set up a working station
competencies.explanation: Antenna, PSU transceiver, ATU.

competencies.statement: I understand SWR and how to use an SWR meter, analyser and Antenna Tuning Unit (ATU)
I have built, tuned, and logged at least 3 QSO’s on a dipole or ¼ wave GP or similar antenna that I have made and tuned myself
I understand EMF, PEP, EIRP, the relative danger of electromagnetic waves at various powers and how to set up an antenna safely
I can name 10 of the main Amateur radio bands and how their propagation might be changed by the time of day, day of year & sun cycle
I understand and can explain the following different antenna types
competencies.explanation: ¼ wave ground plane, Dipole, End Fed Half Wave -EFHW, Random wire, Yagi-Uda.

competencies.statement: I understand the important of good procedure for communicating via amateur radio
competencies.explanation: I have read and abide by the DX code of conduct. I know how to call and answer CQ, how to give signal reports and how to ‘break’ into an existing communication. I know what ‘split’ operation is, how to recognise a station is operating split, and when to use it. I know how to recognise and operate with a DXpedition station, Competition station & normal amateur radio station.

competencies.statement: I understand the importance of a clean signal and how to check if my station is over modulating
competencies.explanation: Radio check or SDR.

competencies.statement: I understand and can use the P=VI equation
I know the meaning and use of Mayday, PanPan and Securite
competencies.explanation: I can use radio communications effectively in an emergency situation (Emergencies L7) and I know how to contact emergency services using Marine VHF C16.

competencies.statement: I understand how to calculate the resistance of a circuit of parallel or in series resistors
I understand how to calculate the capacitance of a circuit of parallel or in series capacitors
I understand how to calculate the inductance of a circuit of parallel or in series inductors
I understand the concept of a tuned circuit and understand how to calculate the frequency of a tuned circuit
I can name and explain the characteristics of 3 different types of coax and or transmission line
I have built a choke and a balun and can explain what they do
I have completed a simple electronics or Arduino/Rasberry Pi project
I have studied the curriculum and have sat the exam and obtained a UK Foundation License
competencies.explanation: No novice license is available yet in Ireland, but ROI scouts can sit the UK exam and obtain a certificate, they cannot get a UK novice license though. OR I have studied the marine VHF license curriculum and have sat the exam and obtained a Marine VHF License (SRC).

competencies.statement: I have completed at least 2 of the following Amateur Radio/Radio Scouting Special Activities with at least 10 QSO’s
competencies.explanation: IOTA, POTA, JOTA, SOTA, DxPedition, AREN exercise, Competition.

competencies.statement: I have built and tuned a multiband antenna with at least 3 bands
competencies.explanation: e.g. nested ¼ waves or fan dipole.

competencies.statement: I have built an electronic gadget and can use a soldering Iron to solder components onto a PCB
I can detect meteors using radio
I have set up an operated on a scout camp or field day event without the use of mains power electricity
I have logged at least 200 QSO’s across a minimum of 3 modes
competencies.explanation: SSB, AM, FM, Digi e.g. FT8, CW.

competencies.statement: I have logged at least 50 different countries (DXCC entities)
I have obtained an Amateur Radio HAREC Class A or B licence, Marine LRC license or UK full license
I have competed in a competition and made >100 verified/scored qso’s
I have supervised a station at a JOTA-JOTI or similar multi station event
I have made a contact over an amateur radio satellite
I have conducted 50 assisted CW QSO’s
competencies.explanation: Using a keyer and skimmer/decoder.

competencies.statement: I have achieved DXCC on at least 4 bands
competencies.explanation: LOTW or QRZ.com certified.

competencies.statement: I have achieved DXCC on at least 6 bands
I have built a simple morse code oscillator and can send my callsign, 599 and 73
I have operated in another country
I can send and receive morse code at 5 wpm or more
I have obtained a Class A licence Harec license or equivalent
I have completed 50 DXCC’s on 160m and 6m
I have completed at least 1 DXCC award on CW, Phone & Digital modes
competencies.explanation: LOTW or QRZ.com certified.

competencies.statement: I can send & receive CW reliably >= 25 wpm
competencies.explanation: Verified by membership of CWOPS or FOC.

competencies.statement: I have completed at least 5 of the following special activities
competencies.explanation: IOTA, POTA, JOTA, SOTA, DxPedition, AREN exercise, Competition (verified by submission of evidence).
